content: Rifampin is a semi-synthetic antibiotic derived from rifamycin SV. It is available in two forms: oral capsules and an injectable formulation. The oral capsules, marketed under the brand name RIFADIN, are available in two strengths: 150 mg and 300 mg of rifampin per capsule. In addition to the active ingredient rifampin, these capsules contain the following inactive ingredients: corn starch, D&C Red No. 28, FD&C Blue No. 1, FD&C Red No. 40, gelatin, magnesium stearate, and titanium dioxide. The injectable formulation, RIFADIN IV, contains 600 mg of rifampin, along with 10 mg of sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate and sodium hydroxide, which is used to adjust the pH of the solution. Rifampin is a red-brown crystalline powder that is very slightly soluble in water at neutral pH. It is freely soluble in chloroform, soluble in ethyl acetate, and soluble in methanol. Its chemical formula is C43H58N4O12. The chemical name of rifampin is: 3-[[(4-methyl-1-piperazinyl)imino]methyl]rifamycin SV 5,6,9,17,19,21-hexahydroxy-23-methoxy-2,4,12,16,20,22-heptamethyl-8-[2,7-(epoxypentadecatrienimino)]naphthofuran-1,11(2H)-dione 21-acetate.
